Validate at the edge, trust nothing from the client: schema-check every request body (Zod, Laravel Form Requests, Joi).
Index the columns you filter and sort on. EXPLAIN the slow query before you rewrite the code.
Queue anything slow (emails, PDFs, imports) and keep web requests fast. Laravel queues + Redis make this easy.
Make CRM status changes explicit state transitions, and log who changed what and when.
Role-based access belongs on the server. Hiding a button is UX, not security.
Prefer idempotent webhooks and imports: the same payload twice should not create two records.
Use database transactions for multi-step writes, such as creating a lead plus its contact and activity.
Keep secrets in environment variables and commit only a .env.example.
Paginate every list endpoint from day one; cursor pagination scales better than offsets.
Debounce search inputs (~300 ms) and cancel stale requests to keep UIs snappy.
Design empty, loading and error states first. They are most of what users actually see.
Bulk imports: validate the whole file, report row-level errors, then commit in chunks.
In React, derive state instead of syncing it. Fewer useEffects, fewer bugs.
Next.js App Router: fetch on the server by default and reach for client components only when you need interactivity.
Tailwind tip: extract repeated class lists into components, not into @apply soup.
Write the README as if you'll forget everything in six months, because you will.
Add a /health endpoint and check it in CI and in Docker healthchecks.
Seed realistic demo data so reviewers can try the app in under a minute.
Use optimistic UI for quick actions, but always reconcile with the server response.
Log with context (user id, request id), not just messages.
Small PRs get reviewed faster and break less. Ship in slices.
Run lint, type-check and tests in CI on every PR; let the robot be the strict reviewer.
Dedupe CRM contacts on normalized email and phone (E.164) before insert, not after.
Version your API (/api/v1) before the first external client depends on it.
Cache expensive reads with explicit invalidation, and measure before and after.
React Native: test on a real low-end device. The simulator hides performance problems.
Prefer UTC in the database and convert to local time only at the edges.
Feature flags let you merge early and release later.
Every background job should be safe to retry.
Measure, don't guess: profile the slow path before optimizing it.
